title: Mission and business context
goal: The organization documents its mission and business context, has leadership approve them, and ties its security risk priorities to them.
note: NIST-only. Mission statement and link to risk priorities; ISO issues and stakeholders do not hold it.

title: Risk direction communicated to those who act on it
goal: The organization delivers its risk direction, methods, roles and decisions to the people who must act on them and keeps evidence that they received it.
note: NIST-only. Shared by atoms that ask for communication of a specific artifact where no base control owns it.

title: Security test and exercise program
goal: The organization plans a program of security tests and exercises that includes critical suppliers where relevant, and records the improvements each one identifies.
note: NIST-only. Program-level plan across penetration, tabletop and recovery tests.

title: Risk appetite, tolerance and response direction
goal: Leadership sets and communicates the amount of risk the organization will accept, turns it into measurable limits, and defines the response options and the criteria for choosing among them.
note: NIST-only. Strategic direction above the per-risk treatment decision.

title: Integration with enterprise risk management
goal: The organization includes cybersecurity and supply chain risks in its enterprise risk process, with defined channels and criteria for raising and escalating them to leadership.
note: NIST-only. Escalation and enterprise reporting of security risk.

title: Policy exceptions and time-limited risk acceptance
goal: The organization approves departures from policy through a defined process, limits each by an expiry or review point, and tracks each open exception to closure.
note: Remainder of UC-RSK-10 for policy exceptions; also NIST-only for the exception process itself.

title: Threat identification and register
goal: The organization identifies internal and external threats, including insiders, records them in a register and keeps that register current from threat information.
note: NIST-only. Threat side of risk assessment.

title: Data flow mapping
goal: The organization maps how data moves between key systems and across internal and external boundaries and keeps those maps current.
note: NIST-only.

title: Asset criticality and priority
goal: The organization ranks its assets by criticality, resources and impact on its mission, in addition to classification, and reviews the ranking.
note: Remainder of UC-AST-04; also NIST-only for ranking every asset.

title: Asset life cycle management
goal: The organization sets security steps for each stage of an asset life cycle, from acquisition or deployment through change to retirement.
note: NIST-only.

title: End-of-life replacement and removal
goal: The organization replaces or formally excepts software and hardware that vendors no longer support, and removes software it does not need.
note: Remainder of UC-PHY-12 for replacement; NIST-only for software end of life and removal.

title: Non-human credential inventory
goal: The organization keeps an inventory of service accounts, API keys, certificates and similar non-human credentials, each with a named owner.
note: Remainder of UC-IAM-02.

title: Identity verification before credential issue
goal: The organization verifies a person's identity, with stronger proof for higher-risk access, before issuing credentials.
note: Remainder of UC-IAM-03.

title: Federation assertion security
goal: The organization requires identity assertions used for single sign-on to be signed, validated by the receiving system, short-lived, and protected by rotated signing keys.
note: NIST-only.

title: Protection of data in use
goal: The organization protects data while it is processed, by keeping secrets out of logs and code, holding them in a controlled store, and isolating one user's or tenant's data from another's.
note: Remainder of UC-CRY-01; also NIST-only for secrets handling and tenant isolation.

title: Authenticity and integrity of acquired hardware and software
goal: The organization checks that hardware and software are genuine and unaltered before it is acquired or put into use.
note: Remainder of UC-NET-08; also NIST-only for hardware and acquisition checks.

title: Vulnerability disclosure intake
goal: The organization gives outside parties a channel to report vulnerabilities, analyzes each report and decides on and records a response.
note: NIST-only.

title: Security steps across the employment life cycle
goal: The organization builds security steps into its HR procedures for onboarding, role change and offboarding, in addition to screening, and confirms they were done.
note: Remainder of UC-PPL-01.

title: Supplier risk management program
goal: The organization runs a documented supplier risk program with stated objectives, assigned accountability and defined responsibilities for suppliers, customers and partners, agreed by its stakeholders.
note: NIST-only. Program, roles and responsibilities for the supply chain.

title: Supplier relationship exit
goal: The organization sets what must happen when a supplier relationship ends, including return or destruction of data and removal of access, and follows it.
note: NIST-only. Cloud exit sits in UC-SUP-06.

title: Third-party roles in incident planning and exercises
goal: The organization names the suppliers and other third parties that take part in incident planning, response and recovery, defines their roles and includes them in exercises.
note: Remainder of UC-INC-01.

title: Approved public statements after incidents
goal: The organization governs public statements about incidents and recovery through an approved procedure that sets who may speak publicly, an approval step and approved wording.
note: NIST-only. Linked to the notification duties control.

title: Critical service identification
goal: The organization identifies the services that customers and other outside parties depend on, decides which are critical by written criteria and tells those parties what it commits to.
note: NIST-only. Input to recovery objectives in UC-RES-02.

title: Dependencies of critical services
goal: The organization maps the external resources and services its critical functions depend on, ranks them, identifies single points of failure and shares the map with those responsible for continuity and risk.
note: NIST-only.

title: Integrity of backups and restored assets
goal: The organization checks backups and other restoration assets for integrity and compromise before using them, verifies restored systems before return to production and confirms normal operation after restoration.
note: NIST-only. Extends restore testing in UC-RES-05.

title: Alert analysis, correlation and routing
goal: The organization analyzes alerts and adverse events under defined procedures, correlates events from several sources, records its conclusions, assigns each alert for follow-up, gives the people who respond access to the analysis platform, and gives analysts asset context during investigation.
note: NIST-only. Split from UC-OPS-03 so monitoring and alert handling are tested apart.

title: Incident recovery and its closure
goal: The organization starts recovery from incident response under set criteria, assigns recovery roles and approvals, carries out and records the recovery actions, and declares the end of recovery against criteria.
note: NIST-only. Split from UC-INC-03 so recovery is tested apart from containment and eradication.
